key_insight: SQD can tolerate aggressive circuit simplification, so much of a VQE ansatz can be pruned or Clifford-rounded without materially harming ground-state energy recovery.
engineering_relevance: This enables smaller, faster quantum chemistry circuits with lower transpilation cost and shallower hardware execution while preserving chemical-accuracy SQD results.
method: Gradient-based operator pruning removes low-impact excitation terms from the VQE ansatz.
Clifford rounding snaps remaining parameters to the nearest Clifford angles to reduce non-Clifford complexity.
Both compressions are applied to a VQE sampling circuit on a qubit-reduced Hamiltonian before SQD post-processing.
evidence_signal: Across 21 molecules, median SQD error stayed within chemical accuracy at 50% compression on both axes, with up to 33× simulation speedup and up to 2.8× transpiled-depth reduction on 6 IBM hardware benchmarks.
watch_item: Compression is benchmarked on selected molecules and circuits, so performance may depend on ansatz quality, molecule instance, and whether enough ground-state overlap remains after simplification.
paper_title: SQD-Enabled Circuit Compression for Resource-Efficient Quantum Chemistry
